title: A diagrammatic field theory of quantum error correction
abstract: We develop a field-theoretic framework for quantum error correction centred on fusion-space codes in unitary fusion categories. Admissible clusters determine total-charge sectors and orthogonal footprint projectors recording locally visible data left by error histories. The central distinction is between diagnostic footprint algebras and syndrome-admissible commuting algebras: the latter can be measured without revealing logical information and resolve chosen error representatives into measured sectors. For such algebras, exact correctability is equivalent to fibrewise Knill--Laflamme conditions, yielding a measure-then-recover factorization. Under a contractible-vacuum locality hypothesis, closed neutral composites give a categorical sufficient criterion for scalar action on the code. In the Ising theory, four $σ$ punctures show that pair-charge footprints can be complementary logical diagnostics and realize an exact one-qubit Clifford shadow. A proper six-$σ$ code instead admits a syndrome-admissible pair-charge measurement and exact recovery from an explicit Majorana bilinear error. A second bilinear has the same measured footprint but differs by a logical bit flip, producing a concrete nontrivial footprint fibre and genuine decoding ambiguity. We also formulate conformal-block likelihood data and compute geometry-dependent Ising four-point weights. For growing code families, we prove a conditional Peierls-type threshold theorem: bounded connected-region growth, local stochastic noise, local neutralizability of small residual components, and componentwise decoder balance imply $\Pr_L(\mathrm{fail})\le C|Ω_L|e^{-cL}$ below a nonzero constant error rate. We conclude with representation-theoretic and algebro-geometric directions involving tube and Hopf algebras, Yangian-type structures, Higgs bundles, spectral curves, Jacobians, and abelian varieties.
summary: This work develops a sophisticated field-theoretic approach to Quantum Error Correction by modeling errors as boundary data ('footprints') in topological theories. It proves key theorems relating measurement compatibility (syndrome-admissibility) to exact correctability and establishes a conditional threshold theorem for noise resilience. The paper bridges quantum information theory with advanced mathematics like conformal field theory and algebraic geometry.
main_problem: Developing a rigorous field-theoretic framework for Quantum Error Correction (QEC) by treating error histories as boundary data ('footprints') within topological or conformal field theory structures.
main_result: The paper establishes that exact correctability is equivalent to a fibrewise Knill–Laflamme condition for syndrome-admissible algebras, and proves a conditional Peierls-type threshold theorem for local noise in growing code families.
method: It employs advanced mathematical tools from unitary fusion categories, conformal field theory (calculating conformal blocks), and diagrammatic techniques (like the ZX-calculus) to translate QEC into an inference problem over physical histories.
model_or_system: The model is general topological/fusion-space codes, exemplified by surface codes and the Ising model. The focus is on how local measurements ('syndromes') constrain the global error history ('footprint').
key_observables: Footprints (locally visible boundary data from errors), Syndrome information (measured projections of the footprint), Conformal-block likelihood data, and Error correction failure probability ($\Pr_L(\mathrm{fail})$).
important_parameters: Error rate ($p$), Code size/geometry ($|Ω_L|$), and the non-zero constant error rate threshold.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on hypotheses such as contractible-vacuum locality, bounded connected-region growth, and local neutralizability for the threshold theorem to hold.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the field-theoretic framework using fusion categories, establishing the core algebraic condition (Knill–Laflamme), demonstrating concrete examples (Ising theory), proving a conditional threshold theorem for noise resilience, and concluding with advanced mathematical generalizations involving Hopf algebras and Higgs bundles.
why_interesting: It provides deep connections between abstract mathematics (category theory, geometry) and practical quantum computation problems like fault tolerance, offering new theoretical tools to analyze error correction beyond standard stabilizer formalisms.
